gap: No result ChatGPT got states that macOS on every Mac, including M-series Pro/Max/M4, lacks DisplayPort Multi-Stream Transport (MST). So a 'single-cable' triple extender like the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 can't drive two separate screens from one USB-C cable on a Mac without Xebec's DisplayLink-based Mac Adapter and driver. Meanwhile the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro gets around this by using two USB-C cables, one per screen, not the 'single USB-C connection' ChatGPT described.
standout_why: I compared four pages. Cited uperfect.com/blogs (8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders) says only that 'base MacBook M1 and M2 chip models only support one external display', with no mechanism and no mention of MST, DisplayLink or DP Alt Mode. Cited rottenwifi.com (11 Best Triple Portable Monitors) and cited sekin.in say a single-cable claim 'can be narrower than it sounds' and that Xebec's Mac adapter 'may be sold separately', but neither mentions MST or explains why. Uncited workcocoon.com mentions no M1/M2 limit, MST, DisplayLink or the Trio 3 Pro. None of them say the limit applies to Pro/Max and M4/M5 Macs too, and none say the Trio 3 Pro connects with two cables. ChatGPT's answers repeated 'single USB-C connection' for the Trio 3 Pro and 'single-cable setup' for the Xebec without these limits.
decides: For a Mac buyer, this changes the pick. Xebec's single-cable design only works on a Mac with the extra $59 DisplayLink adapter and driver, a cost and a dependency ChatGPT left out of its $699 'best premium travel' pick. The Trio 3 Pro's two-cable design is native on any Mac with two DP-capable USB-C ports: M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and M4/M5, per Macworld. Base M1/M2 Macs (Apple: 'One external display') still need Mobile Pixels' driver software whichever extender they use. For Windows buyers whose USB-C ports support DP Alt Mode, the single-cable design works as advertised, so the Trio 3 Pro stays the overall pick.

findings.label: Why a single cable can't drive both screens on a Mac
findings.value: Apple does not support Multi-Stream Transport (MST); Mac users need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter (DisplayLink chips) plus the free DisplayLink driver
findings.source_title: Xebec Tri-Screen 3 review – Serious Insights (Daniel W. Rasmus, 2026-05-06)
findings.note: Daniel W. Rasmus wrote: 'Apple does not support Multi-Stream Transport (MST)… in the way this product requires for a single-cable dual-display setup' and 'Xebec's adapter uses DisplayLink chips and requires the free' driver. He says the single-cable design is 'the feature' on Windows, ChromeOS and Linux with USB-C DP Alt Mode or Thunderbolt, and that Mac owners 'do not get the cleanest version of the product unless they also buy the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter.' I could not open Xebec's own adapter page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Connection method
findings.value: Two USB-C cables (one per screen, 20 in each); no driver needed if the laptop has two DP-enabled USB-C ports
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Simon Jary describes 'the included two USB-C cables' and quotes the manual: 'if your laptop has two DP enabled USB-C ports … driver installation is not necessary.' He says M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and any M4/M5 MacBook work without the software.

findings.label: Base M1/M2 and MacBook Neo requirement
findings.value: Need Mobile Pixels' free driver software (Jary: 'rather like DisplayLink') to run both screens
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld
findings.note: Jary: 'plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs plus the new MacBook Neo are limited to connecting just a single monitor… will need to download and install free software.'

findings.label: Brightness and pass-through on laptop power
findings.value: Screens can't reach maximum brightness on laptop power alone; a power adapter on a Trio USB-C port gives full brightness and up to 65 W pass-through, but pass-through needs the software install
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld

findings.label: Base Apple M2 MacBook Air external display limit
findings.value: One external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: From Apple's spec sheet. This is why any two-screen extender needs a software or DisplayLink path on base-chip Macs.
